articles.headline: Premier League live updates: Aston Villa host league leaders Man City
articles.description: Aston Villa host Premier League leaders Manchester City as another weekend of European soccer gets underway.
articles.body:
We're back with another action-packed weekend of European soccer!

We kick things off in the Premier League, as Aston Villa welcome league leaders Manchester City, who are 100% this season, to Villa Park in our first match of the day. Later, defending champions Arsenal host Everton at the Emirates Stadium, while Coventry City take on Fulham.

We wrap up the Premier League slate with a London derby, as Xabi Alonso's Chelsea face Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge.

Elsewhere, Napoli host AS Roma in a huge Serie A showdown, while Borussia Dortmund welcome Eintracht Frankfurt to Signal Iduna Park.

Enjoy all the action from Saturday's matches across Europe.

articles.headline: NFL House in Paris closes ahead of street protests in French capital
articles.description: PARIS -- The NFL closed its "NFL House" in Paris on Saturday as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up.
articles.body:
PARIS -- The NFL closed its "NFL House" in Paris on Saturday as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up.

The league announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning through its "OnePass" app and it came a day after closing its pop-up NFL shop - in both cases citing "potential accessibility issues."

Security concerns have overshadowed the NFL's debut in Paris. The New Orleans Saints will play the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in the league's first-ever regular-season game in France.

Also Saturday, the Saints announced that " Saints House has been postponed until Sunday."

Events planned Saturday at NFL House included "French Athletes in Football" and "From the Field to the Community."

Major museums including the Louvre and Orsay Museum are closed Saturday, though tourists were lined up to enter Notre Dame Cathedral. French authorities are intent on preventing a repeat of recent violent unrest.

The U.S. State Department this week issued a security alert that cautioned "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" to "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings" because of protests.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said this week that preparations were made in consultation with U.S. and French authorities. Street protests, he said, "are not unusual in France."

On Friday, French President Emmanuel Macron met with Goodell along with Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers owners Art Rooney II at the Élysée Palace to "discuss Sunday's game and the long-term future of the NFL in Paris."

The NFL said Friday that its pop-up shop in the city center would be closed Saturday but that fans could use an alternative shop set up at Stade de France, located north of the city in Saint-Denis.

A weekend event for Steelers fans was canceled Thursday because of security concerns.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Chelsea, Bayern, Barcelona battle for Brighton defender
articles.description: Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Barcelona are targeting Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic has Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Barcelona on his trail, while AS Roma and AC Milan are interested in signing Real Madrid forward Endrick. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Barcelona are targeting Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, according to TEAMtalk. Vuskovic, 19, only moved to the south coast this summer for an initial £46 million, having spent last season on loan at Hamburg from Tottenham Hotspur. The Croatia international is considered one of the top young defenders in Europe but is focused on helping his new side battle for a spot in the UEFA Champions League for now.

- AS Roma and AC Milan are interested in signing Real Madrid forward Endrick in January, according to Marca. A departure remains on the table for the Brazil international, despite José Mourinho publicly stating he will stay, with Roma considered a particularly realistic destination as his limited playing time continues at the Bernabéu.

- Atlético Madrid are open to triggering their €25 million option to sign Juventus striker Jonathan David permanently, according to Sky Germany. The 26-year-old, who has three goals in five league games this season, is receptive to remaining in Spain beyond his loan, with talks planned between the clubs.

- Arsenal and Liverpool have stepped up their interest in Galatasaray attacking midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, per TEAMtalk. Both clubs sent scouts to watch the 21-year-old score in a 4-2 win over Lille, with Manchester United, Chelsea, and Manchester City also monitoring him. The Russia international has a contract which contains a €60 million release clause.

- Aston Villa will choose not to sign Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho permanently unless his performances improve, Football Insider reports. Villa are willing to limit the winger's game time to prevent triggering an appearance-based obligation included in his loan deal, much like they did with Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott.

- Arsenal are planning a potential double move for Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Can Uzun and Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi. (Ekrem Konur)

articles.headline: José Mourinho backs himself ahead of El Clasico vs. Barcelona: 'Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies'
articles.description: José Mourinho backed himself to deliver at Real Madrid ahead of Sunday's high-stakes El Clásico with LaLiga leaders Barcelona, insisting that "Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies."
articles.body:
MADRID -- José Mourinho backed himself to deliver at Real Madrid ahead of Sunday's high-stakes El Clásico with LaLiga leaders Barcelona, insisting that "Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies."

Madrid are already six points behind Barça in the table -- after defeats at Real Betis and Atletico Madrid -- but they've had a 100% winning record since the international break, with victories over Villarreal, Roma, Sevilla and RB Leipzig.

Mourinho won one LaLiga title, a Copa del Rey and a Spanish Supercopa in his previous, three-year spell at Madrid between 2010 and 2013, although he was unable to land the ultimate prize of the Champions League.

"No," he said in a news conference on Saturday, when asked if Sunday's game at Camp Nou was a litmus test for this team's ability to succeed. "Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies."

Barcelona have won nine games out of nine in LaLiga so far this season, but were beaten 4-2 by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League in midweek.

Mourinho said that result -- coupled with Madrid's improved performance against Leipzig -- was unlikely to affect the Clásico, which he described as a match which makes "the football-loving world come to a standstill."

"If people thought a week ago that we were going to get thrashed by Barça, they'll still think the same," he said. "People speaking highly of Barcelona doesn't affect me.

"There are moments that deserve praise, because they do some very good things. In our case, we're being viewed as a finished article... but we're nowhere near that stage.

"We are far from being the finished article. We're in the early stages, a phase where the coach is getting to know the squad, analyzing things, and defining our path. It doesn't seem fair to me to compare a team at this stage of development to one that has been together for two, three years."

Madrid's only high-profile absentee is Vinícius Júnior, who is suspended.

For Barça, the focus as ever will be on star winger Lamine Yamal.

"They're all good players," Mourinho said, when asked if he had a specific plan for Yamal.

"He's a great player, and great players deserve respect. But there's a difference between showing respect and changing your plans, structures, or forgetting your own identity. We won't do that for him our any other opponent."

articles.headline: Amen Thompson stuffs Wemby's last-second shot as Rockets hold off Spurs
articles.description: Rockets guard Amen Thompson blocked Victor Wembanyama at the rim to prevent a potential tying bucket as the Rockets beat the Spurs 114-110.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas -- Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson couldn't quite explain what happened after sealing a 114-110 victory over the San Antonio Spurs by swatting away a last-gasp attempt at the rim by Victor Wembanyama.

In the aftermath of the game-saving play, Rockets forward Kevin Durant scurried over in excitement to deliver Thompson a message Friday as the sellout crowd at Moody Center groaned in disbelief.

"I said, 'What the f--- is wrong with him, thinking he was just going to lay it up so easily?'" Durant recalled.

"I don't know," Thompson shot back.

With five seconds remaining and Houston clinging to a 112-110 lead, Spurs point guard De'Aaron Fox floated a pass over Rockets forward Jabari Smith Jr. to Wembanyama, just as the big man spun toward the basket outside the restricted area. Wembanyama soared for what ends with a dunk in most cases. But Wembanyama's eight-foot wingspan couldn't clear Thompson's seven-foot reach and pogo-stick leaping ability.

"I just knew they were going to try to get probably me or one of the other smaller guys on him," Thompson said. "I jump pretty high, so I wouldn't try to keep ducking [in on] me."

Thompson smacked Wembanyama's attempt into the waiting hands of Fred VanVleet, who iced the game with a pair of free throws.

"Man, what an incredible block," Durant said. "It was just insane, man. As soon as your feet hit the ground, to be able to bounce back up so quick, that's rare in any human. To be 6-7, dunk the ball and block shots like a center is insane."

Thompson finished with a team-worst minus-12 on the box score. But what transpired on the floor told a different story for the 23-year-old, who finished with 20 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and a pair of steals.

"We did a really good job of switching and denying some catches, pushed [Wembanyama] off his spot, did his work early instead of getting ducked in like we did quite a few times," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said. "And from there, he uses athleticism and God-given ability there and did a hell of a job one-on-one with him in the post."

Thompson worked Wembanyama on the offensive end, too. With 1:13 left in the third quarter, Thompson cut to the basket for a two-hand jam over the Frenchman off an assist by Durant. Wembanyama fouled Thompson on the play, and the Rockets guard nailed the and-1 free throw to give Houston a nine-point lead.

"That's low-key getting dunked on, right?" Thompson said, smiling.

Thompson and Durant scored 20 points apiece, but Rockets center Alperen Sengun dominated Wembanyama and the rest of the Spurs bigs to pour in a game-high 29 points with seven rebounds and seven assists. The performance marked his 35th career game with 25 points, five rebounds and five assists, tying Steve Francis for the second-most such games by a Rockets player before age 25.

Sengun scored 18 points in the second half, including 14 in the fourth quarter, to help Houston get off to its first 2-0 start since 2017-18.

articles.headline: Will Niners have edge with ex-Falcons coach facing Penix?
articles.description: With all of the familiarity between Morris and the Falcons, Sunday's game should come down to execution.
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Bijan Robinson has maintained a close relationship with Raheem Morris. It makes sense. Morris was the Atlanta Falcons' head coach for two of the first three seasons of Robinson's career.

On Sunday, the two men will meet again under different circumstances.

Robinson will be helping to lead the Falcons' offense as one of the top running backs in the league. Morris, who has called Robinson the best player in the NFL multiple times, will be back in Atlanta as the San Francisco 49ers' defensive coordinator. Morris was fired as Atlanta's coach in January after back-to-back eight-win campaigns.

Robinson said he spoke to Morris just a few weeks ago, and he's relishing the chance to face off against a man he calls a "father figure" to him.

"He's always going to be family to me no matter if we compete or not," Robinson said. "But yeah, man, he still talks to all of his players, because that's just who he is."

Morris is glad Penix has recovered from the torn left ACL that ended his season last year on Nov. 16.

"He's back healthy and he's probably everything that you thought and hoped for as far as being a play-action passer, a guy that can push the ball down the field, can make all the throws, go through the whole process," Morris said. "Just one of those guys that I have a lot of appreciation for and love for."

The Falcons players on offense who have been here the past several years will be going up against a defense run by a man who knows them all too well.  And that 49ers defense has been potent regardless of opponent familiarity. San Francisco is allowing the fourth-fewest points per game (18.3) and the fifth-fewest yards per game (300).

Atlanta (2-4) must perform against Morris and the undefeated Niners or risk losing three straight games and moving to 0-4 at home. A fifth loss in the first seven games is not how the Falcons wanted to start off under new head coach Kevin Stefanski.

The Falcons' biggest issue on offense is one the Chicago Bears exploited last week in a 31-23 Falcons loss. The Bears pressured quarterback Michael Penix Jr. 46.2% of the time, the highest rate Penix has faced this season. Chicago sacked Penix five times and blitzed on more than half of his dropbacks.

The results were not good. For the season, Penix has the worst EPA per dropback under quick pressure in the NFL (-1.17). He is 3-of-15 for 17 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions in those scenarios.

With no pressure at all, Penix has the fourth-best EPA per dropback in the league (0.40). So, it is imperative that the Falcons figure out how to better protect him.

"Any game you go into, you want to protect your quarterback," Stefanski said. "And I think you protect your quarterback literally with the protection, but also you protect the quarterback with how guys get open, how we get the ball out of our hands, how we run the ball, all those type of things."

No defensive coordinator knows Penix better than Morris. He was part of the regime

articles.headline: Fernando Mendoza is embracing being Raiders' latest Hispanic QB
articles.description: The rookie's next chapter is inspired by the legacies of a Hispanic coach, QB and a Raiders' fan base embracing the culture.
articles.body:
IN HIGH SCHOOL in 2021, Fernando Mendoza watched former Texas A&M quarterback Zach Calzada, a Cuban American like himself, and wondered about other Cubans and Hispanic quarterbacks who played at the next level. More importantly, he wanted to know how many of them had success in the NFL, even winning Super Bowls --- a dream of his.

A Google search opened Mendoza's eyes. He researched Tom Flores and Jim Plunkett, who are considered trailblazers for Latinos in the sport. Flores (Mexican American) was the first Hispanic quarterback in the NFL in 1960 when he debuted for the Oakland Raiders -- who are now based in Las Vegas. Plunkett, also Mexican American, was a college standout at Stanford, winning the Heisman Trophy in 1970 before being drafted by the New England Patriots with the first overall pick in 1971.

Plunkett is the first Hispanic American player to win the Heisman Trophy and be drafted No. 1.

Flores and Plunkett simultaneously became the first Hispanic coach and first Hispanic quarterback to win a Super Bowl. The duo helped the Raiders defeat the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl XV in 1981 -- the first of two Super Bowls that they won together. Plunkett was named the game's Most Valuable Player.

"To see that example [and] to know whatever I am doing, it is possible, meant a great deal to me," Mendoza told ESPN.

As the Raiders' No. 1 pick in April's draft, Mendoza is now doing more than just viewing Flores and Plunkett as inspirational figures. Mendoza is continuing their legacy. Should Mendoza start for the Raiders, he'll join another No. 1 pick in Carolina Panthers QB Bryce Young as the only starting quarterbacks of Hispanic descent in the NFL this season.

Regardless of whether he wants to be, he is a beacon of hope for the Raiders, with a fairly large Hispanic fan base. Flores and Plunkett symbolize the franchise's glory days, and they believe Mendoza can help bring the team back to relevance. Mendoza understands the role bestowed upon him can be pressure and a privilege. At the same time, it's added motivation for him to have a career that can be an inspiration for others who look like him.

"It's a great sense of pride knowing that it's been done before and it can be done; winning a championship [while] being Hispanic as the focal point," Mendoza said. "However, it's also a great deal of pressure, and that's something I take upon myself whenever I make decisions."

WHEN MENDOZA ARRIVED in Las Vegas after April's 2026 NFL draft, the magnitude of his presence was evident. The Raiders have not been to the postseason since 2021, which was the last year they finished with a winning record. The organization hasn't been to the Super Bowl since 2002 and hasn't hoisted the Vince Lombardi Trophy since Plunkett and Flores led the Raiders to a victory over the Washington Commanders in Super Bowl XVIII in 1984.

articles.headline: Inside the silent messages Boye Mafe sends every game day
articles.description: The Bengals defensive end uses sign language to say "I love you" to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- Before the chaos of each game unfolds, Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Boye Mafe has a conversation that centers him in a special place.

He closes his eyes and starts talking to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018. And in those moments, Mafe lays out his vision for what's about to unfold.

I know you're watching over me. I want to put on a show for you. I love you and this is what I'm going to do for you.

Then he'll wrap up the message by using American Sign Language to say "I love you" before he continues the rest of his pregame routine. Mafe does the same after each sack.

But it's about more than signs. Everything Mafe does is about what he signals. From those messages to Bola, to his pregame outfits, to how he plays, it's all about honoring the systems and structures that built him into one of the NFL's leading pass rushers and a Super Bowl champion.

"I try not to let circumstances dictate who I am," Mafe told ESPN. "At the end of the day, I am who I am and I want to be true to who I am."

That doesn't come easily. Mafe, the son of proud Nigerians, grapples with a phenomenon that is common among those with generational ties to other places -- the more time passes, the harder it is to stay connected to those roots.

But all it takes is one glance on game day to see just how strong those ties are.

How Boye Mafe's mother impacted her community

To fully understand why Mafe signs to his late mother requires understanding his upbringing in the western suburbs of Minneapolis.

Mafe and his siblings often communicate via American Sign Language. Starting with his older sister, Tayo, they all decided to study it in high school as their alternative language. And over the years the practice has stuck, even during games. Once, Tayo recalled signing to Mafe when he suffered an injury at Minnesota. He quickly signaled back that it wasn't anything serious.

Of all Mafe's six siblings, he is the one who spent the most time in their mother's seamstress shop on 1110 Lowery Avenue in North Minneapolis. There, Bola did more than mend clothes. She served as a cultural hub for many, not just Nigerians or those with Yoruba roots.

And she invested in the community. She volunteered at a battered women's shelter, made vests for Mafe's entire church choir and often let her customers have some extended credit.

"She had a lot of patience because sometimes people couldn't pay and she was like, 'Oh, pay me later,'" said Angie Onayiga, one of Bola's longtime friends. "She still gave them the clothes, sold things for them."

When Bola was diagnosed with cancer while Boye was in high school, the bond between mother and son deepened. Boye and his brother Domi did everything they could to make sure Bola was as comfortable as possible as the disease progressed.

How she fought the disease made a lasting impact on Boye.

articles.headline: NFL Week 7 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
articles.description: Touchdowns for Tucker Kraft and Germie Bernard? Cardinals pull another upset? Revenge game for Trey Hendrickson? Let's predict 15 things for Week 7.
articles.body:
Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Bears beat the Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Can the Cardinals pull off an upset for the second straight week? What could Packers tight end Tucker Kraft's stat line look like against the Lions? Is Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee a sneaky play in fantasy? And how many sacks will Ravens edge rusher Trey Hendrickson have against his former team?

Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Arizona Cardinals +4.5 (+195 moneyline) vs. Denver Broncos

The Broncos haven't shown they can pull away when ahead this season. Denver is averaging only 3.4 yards per carry (third lowest in the league), and quarterback Bo Nix has thrown for just 230 yards over the past two games combined. Despite a strong showing against the Rams, Arizona's pass defense has given up plenty of explosive plays in 2026. But Denver rarely throws downfield to take advantage.

The Broncos' defense should be a tough matchup for Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett, so I'm not expecting a big offensive day from the Cardinals. But this matchup looks like it will be decided by a field goal, and Arizona could come out on top.

Kansas City Chiefs +2.5 (+120 moneyline) at Seattle Seahawks

Kansas City has the defense to keep this close even if Seattle slows down QB Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs create pressure on nearly 39% of dropbacks, and QB Sam Darnold has completed only 38% of his throws under pressure this season. Seattle's struggles with run blocking could leave him handling too many difficult passing downs.

Offensively, running back Kenneth Walker III faces a tough rushing matchup against his former team, but Seattle has had issues covering RBs as receivers. That gives Kansas City another way to move the ball and win this outright.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Tucker Kraft, TE, Green Bay Packers: 9 targets, 7 receptions, 87 receiving yards, 1 TD

Kraft has the benefit of going against a Lions defense that has allowed 27% of its targets to opposing tight ends, the second-highest rate in the league. But it gets better. Based on player tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats, Detroit linebackers Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes and Jack Campbell all bite on play-action more than average. The Packers haven't used play-action a ton this season, but Kraft could be the beneficiary whenever they do Sunday.

articles.headline: Nottingham Forest rue 'wrong' red card call, missed chances in Ipswich draw
articles.description: Nottingham Forest lamented the referee's decision not to reduce Ipswich Town to 10 men in the second half, as well a number of missed chances in front of goal, after a 1-1 draw at Portman Road.
articles.headlineJa: ノッティンガム・フォレスト、イプスウィッチ戦の引き分けに「誤った」退場判定と決定機逸失を悔やむ
articles.descriptionJa: ポートマン・ロードでの試合が1-1の引き分けに終わった後、ノッティンガム・フォレストは、後半にイプスウィッチ・タウンを10人にしなかった審判の判定や、ゴール前での数多くの決定機を逃したことを嘆いた。
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest were left ruing the referee's decision not to reduce Ipswich Town to 10 men in the second half, as well a number of missed chances in front of goal, after a 1-1 draw at Portman Road on Friday.

The result lifted Forest out of the relegation zone but extended their winless run to four matches.

The big talking point was the 48th minute decision not to send off Issa Diop after he felled James McAtee as he headed towards the Ipswich goal. The video referee looked at the decision and Diop was yellow-carded.

"It was the wrong decision but we couldn't have played a more dominant second half," Forest coach Oliver Glasner told Sky Sports. "We created enough chances to decide the game and that's why I will never blame the referee.

"I liked that he went to the screen, this is the right procedure. It was wrong [decision] but he didn't do it on purpose."

On a blustery night, Forest played with the wind behind them during the first half and it was a swirling ball that led to the opener.

Daniel Muñoz threw in a high cross from the right and Neco Williams was unmarked in the box and guided his volley into the net.

Ipswich drew level four minutes before halftime when Nikola Milenkovic was caught in possession by Julio Enciso. The Paraguayan midfielder ran on to calmly slot the ball past diving goalkeeper Matz Sels.

Forest had the bulk of the chances in a gritty second period but could not make its superiority count.

"We have had so many good performances recently and we haven't been able to get the final three points and get over the line," Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White said. "Again tonight we had a lot of chances.

"The first half we were in control, then they were in control. But the second half we dominated completely and should have won the game, in my eyes. If we keep up these performances like this then the wins are going to have to come."

Forest have only one win in eight Premier League fixtures, which was also the case in the 2025-26 campaign and it led to owner Evangelos Marinakis dismissing Nuno Espirito Santo and Ange Postecoglou by this point last year.

However, Glasner struck a relaxed tone about the direction his team were heading in.

"Yes, the result, I think, doesn't reflect the performance, but I don't know a different solution than just to keep going because everyone sees, everyone feels we are on the right track, with the way we play, the way we create chances and also the way we defend," he told a news conference.

"[Now] it's supporting the players, keep the confidence and just waiting for this click. Maybe it's an own goal or a deflected ball like we lost last week because then the results will follow the performances."

Ipswich moved up one place to ninth in the table and manager Gary O'Neil acknowledged they had to dig deep to frustrate Forest.

articles.headline: Roberto De Zerbi defends Spurs' 'high level' medical staff amid injury crisis
articles.description: Roberto De Zerbi has defended Tottenham's medical staff despite an ongoing injury crisis.
articles.headlineJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ監督、負傷者続出の中でもスパーズの「ハイレベルな」医療スタッフを擁護
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ監督は、負傷者が相次ぐ危機的な状況にありながらも、トッテナムの医療スタッフを擁護しました。
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi has defended Tottenham's medical staff despite an ongoing injury crisis.

Spurs travel to rivals Chelsea on Saturday night, but will be without several key figures and Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison are doubts following disrupted training this week after they featured in Monday's win over Coventry.

Destiny Udogie remains sidelined and Tosin Adarabioyo may not recover in time. Pedro Porro is available in a welcome boost, but fitness problems have been a frequent issue for Tottenham this season and during recent campaigns.

Yet De Zerbi said: "It's football. I am convinced our medical staff this season is high level.

"I follow them. I believe in them. I have big confidence because I know how they are working.

"I think they are good enough to believe in them. Nothing more. We are suffering a normal situation in football."

De Zerbi went on to highlight three players and the unique circumstances surrounding their fitness issues.

Porro "suffered in the World Cup the muscular problem of the hamstring," which was behind his absence at the start of the season.

The Spanish right-back returned against Aston Villa, but "pushed to come back before the right time and he suffered another injury."

De Zerbi pointed out: "What is the responsibility of the medical team?"

On the sidelined Lucas Bergvall, De Zerbi added: "In the beginning of the [Manchester United] game, in the tackle, he turned his knee and felt pain.

"He finished the game and the day after he felt pain. What is the responsibility of the medical staff? Nothing.

"[Andy] Robertson played four games in a row with the national team.

"[Against Coventry] was fatigued. It's normal fatigue for a player who played six games in 20 days.

"At the end of this season we make the total report and we analyse the situation but so far we can't say anything bad about the medical staff or another reason."

- Tottenham's Roberto De Zerbi denies Chelsea raids of former club Brighton are extra motivation for derby

- Tottenham beat Arsenal in ex-footballer boxing fight, Nile Ranger pulls out

- James Maddison apologises to Coventry fans for Tottenham goal celebration

What cannot be debated is Tottenham's horrendous away record at Chelsea which includes only one win in 41 matches at Stamford Bridge but De Zerbi, who won there with Brighton in 2023, has a positive experience to lean on.

"When I was the coach of Foggia. League Three against League Two, many, many times Foggia did not win in the [Bari] stadium but it was one motivation more, not one pressure more," De Zerbi said. "And yes, we won [in 2015]."

articles.headline: USMNT's Scally scores, helps Gladbach avoid worst-ever Bundesliga start
articles.description: Borussia Mönchengladbach avoided becoming the first team in Bundesliga history to lose seven straight games to start the season, thanks to a 3-2 win at Stuttgart on Friday.
articles.headlineJa: 米代表スカリーが得点、グラッドバッハがブンデスリーガ史上最悪の開幕戦連敗を回避
articles.descriptionJa: ボルシア・メンヒェングラートバッハは、金曜日のシュトゥットガルト戦に3-2で勝利し、ブンデスリーガ史上初の開幕7連敗という不名誉を免れました。
articles.body:
Borussia Mönchengladbach avoided becoming the first team in Bundesliga history to lose seven straight games to start the season, thanks to a 3-2 win at Stuttgart on Friday.

United States defender Joe Scally led the way for Gladbach with a goal and an assist as they got their long-awaited first points of the campaign.

- Bayern Munich coach Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

- Dortmund's new app rewards fans who lock phones while at stadium

- Musah is back in Milan, back in midfield and back in contention for the USMNT

Gladbach came into the game with a club record goals against tally of minus-20 after six games, and they looked set for a seventh straight loss when they went behind after six minutes through Ermedin Demirović.

However, in one of the turnarounds of the Bundesliga so far, Scally's fourth goal of the season via a deft backheel brought Gladbach level seven minutes before halftime. Shuto Machino then gave the visitors the unlikeliest of leads six minutes into the second period.

Having set up Gladbach's second goal, Wael Mohya made sure of the points with a header from a Scally cross midway through the second half. It was the 17-year-old's second goal in two games.

Demirović pulled a goal back for the home side with seven minutes left but it was not enough.

"It's an amazing feeling to finally get our first win of the season," Mohya said. "We came here determined to get something from the game, so I'm absolutely delighted that we managed to do that.

"Being able to help the team with an assist and a goal makes it even better. The coach always tells us to fight and give everything for the team. Today we saw that all that hard work pays off. We need to build on this performance and take the momentum into the next few games."

Despite the win, Gladbach remain at the foot of the Bundesliga table. Stuttgart are 14th, ahead of the rest of the weekend's action.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Ipswich earn draw with Forest as Delap misfires on return
articles.description: Liam Delap fired a blank on his return to Ipswich with Nottingham Forest forced to settle for a 1-1 draw despite a dominant display at Portman Road.
articles.headlineJa: イプスウィッチ、フォレストと引き分け。復帰したデラップは得点ならず
articles.descriptionJa: リアム・デラップはイプスウィッチへの復帰戦で得点を挙げることができず、ノッティンガム・フォレストはポートマン・ロードで圧倒的な試合展開を見せたものの、1-1の引き分けに終わった。
articles.body:
Liam Delap fired a blank on his return to Ipswich with Nottingham Forest forced to settle for a 1-1 draw despite a dominant display at Portman Road.

Delap's 12-goal haul for Ipswich during the 2024-25 campaign earned a big-money move to Chelsea, but he returned to his old club with Forest on Friday with only two Premier League strikes to his name since he departed the Suffolk club.

Any hope of rediscovering that past form failed to materialise and Delap sent over a gilt-edged chance with 16 minutes left to ensure Forest remain with a haul of only one league victory from eight fixtures under Oliver Glasner.

Glasner will wonder how after Neco Williams' deservedly put the visitors in front in the 13th minute before Nikola Milenkovic gifted Gary O'Neil's side an equaliser with a poor back pass, which allowed Julio Enciso to level after 41 minutes.

Forest looked the more likely to grab a second-half winner and were frustrated that Issa Diop avoided a red card for a 47th-minute lunge on James McAtee, but Glasner in the end had to settle for a point.

Glasner stuck with Delap despite his costly misses at Crystal Palace and almost watched the away side score in the sixth minute.

Jair Cunha went close before Delap lashed well wide after good play by fit-again Morgan Gibbs-White.

While Forest started the day second from bottom, the visitors regularly belied their lowly position and broke the deadlock in classic Glasner fashion.

Delap initially held up well versus Diop, then Gibbs-White beat Dara O'Shea to the ball and played in Daniel Muñoz, who picked out fellow wing back Williams to send a right-footed volley past Christian Walton.

It was trademark Glasner and while Enciso curled a free kick over for Ipswich soon after, Forest remained dominant with Gibbs-White off target before only Leif Davis' excellent clearance on the line denied the England midfielder.

However, with four minutes of the first half left, Forest and specifically Milenkovic gifted Ipswich a leveller.

O'Shea's long ball was brought down by Milenkovic but his pass back to Matz Sels was weak and Enciso raced clear before he found the bottom corner.

VAR took centre stage at the start of the second half when referee Thomas Bramall inexplicably failed to penalise Diop for hauling down McAtee before he decided upon review to hand out only a yellow card.

Glasner's men failed to make the most of the subsequent free kick and yet went close on the hour mark with a Williams' shot blocked before Murillo's effort on the turn was saved.

Murillo and then Dan Ndoye went close in quick succession -- Davis again forced to produce a key intervention in front of goal.

Then Delap's big moment arrived but he headed over after Abdoul Ouattara's miscued clearance and then sent a 30-yard piledriver fractionally wide.

Forest lost Williams to a worrying arm injury minutes later and there was still time for Callum Hudson-Odoi to drill wide for the visitors before Ipswich substitute Jack Clarke fired
